title: Windows binary is installed into the data-supplier's folder without DLL search-order hardening (possible DLL planting)
description: The documented install puts the Windows .exe (or the .scr when 'Test'ed from its download folder) into the same folder as the third-party SCRANTIC.SCR/RESOURCE.* files, which users typically extract from an archive the data supplier controls. Windows resolves non-KnownDLL static imports and bare-name LoadLibrary calls from the application directory first, and the build sets neither /DEPENDENTLOADFLAG:0x800 nor SetDefaultDllDirectories. If the shipped binary imports any non-KnownDLL (possible via winit/softbuffer/cpal: dwmapi.dll, uxtheme.dll, avrt.dll, propsys.dll...), an archive that also ships such a DLL would execute native code as the user, raising the data supplier from 'malformed data' to code execution. The System32 .scr install is not affected.
claimed_root_cause: Install instructions couple the executable's application directory (DLL search location) with the folder holding third-party data files (app_dir() is both exe and data/INI location), and the release build does not restrict dependent-DLL resolution to System32.

trace.description: Users put the .exe in the same folder as the three third-party data files.
Data, INI and screenshot directory is the executable's directory.
winit/softbuffer/rodio pull in Win32 imports beyond kernel32/user32; KnownDLL membership not visible.
Only Windows link customization embeds resources; no /DEPENDENTLOADFLAG:0x800.

evidence.description: Put the .exe in the same folder as the original files.
Right-click the .scr and choose Test runs it from its current folder.
embed_resource only; no DLL search hardening.
Manifest declares Common-Controls 6 only; non-screensaver .exe embeds none.

blockers: The PE import table of the released Windows .exe/.scr cannot be produced here (no dependency sources, no Windows toolchain); unknown whether any import or runtime LoadLibrary is outside KnownDLLs.
Windows loader behaviour (KnownDLLs, SxS redirection) is a runtime OS fact not observable in this Linux sandbox.

validation_plan.local: On an offline Windows 10/11 VM: cargo build --release (and --features screensaver) with the pinned toolchain; dumpbin /imports on both binaries and list imports not in HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs nor api-ms-win-*. Copy the exe into a fresh folder with dummy data files and run under Process Monitor (Operation=CreateFile, Path ends with .dll) to record DLLs first probed in the app folder. For a bounded proof, place a benign stub DLL with that name that only writes a marker file in %TEMP% and exits; confirm the marker; remove it. Verify the fix: build.rs emits cargo:rustc-link-arg=/DEPENDENTLOADFLAG:0x800 for MSVC Windows targets.
